prompt: They say email is easiest because they are on site. Payroll runs tomorrow.

choices.label: On site plus a deadline means do it.
On site means they can use the portal.
Reply, and update if they say yes.

prompt: You replied, and the same mailbox confirmed the new account.

choices.label: A confirmation is the check.
The mailbox may be the attacker.
Update it so the run is not late.

prompt: The text says you will be reimbursed for the cards.

choices.label: Reimbursed means it is internal.
The codes are cash. Call a known number.
Text back and ask which store.

prompt: You call the number you already have. They did not send the text.

choices.label: Buy the cards anyway. It was close.
Do not buy. Report the number.
Send one code as a test.

prompt: The approver is out. The batch is tomorrow. Your coworker entered the change.

choices.label: Cover them. You trust them.
One person still cannot finish it.
Split the payment so it fits your limit.

prompt: Both halves of a split go out the same day, to the same new account.

choices.label: Same day means it is one payment.
That is how a limit gets dodged.
It is fine if the vendor is old.

prompt: Where should a pay-account change be made?

choices.label: In the mail thread, so there is a record.
In the payroll system, or face to face.
In chat, if you both are online.

prompt: A request not to call back is attached to a payment.

choices.label: They are busy. Skip the call.
That is the reason to use the known number.
Text the same thread instead.

prompt: The vendor, on the number already on file, says the bank did not change.

choices.label: Approve it. Your coworker was sure.
Stop the change. Nothing has to leave.
Pay half while you think.

prompt: The real person asks where their pay is. You changed it from the email.

choices.label: They must have mistyped the account.
The mailbox was not them.
Wait one more cycle.
